chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfaly, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

A man came to the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) and said, 'I have earned wealth; I closed my eyes in seeking it, [mixing] the permissible and the prohibited. I intend repentance, but I do not know which part is permissible and which is prohibited, and they have become mixed up for me.' The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said, 'Give in charity a fifth of your wealth, for Allah, Exalted is His Name, is pleased with the fifth from the things, and the rest of the wealth is permissible for you.'
ai.seo_question: How to purify mixed halal and haram wealth according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this foundational hadith from Al-Kafi, Imam Ali (AS) provides a practical legal solution for those whose wealth is a mixture of halal and haram, advising the payment of Khums as a purifying deduction. This ruling highlights the Shia scholarly view that Khums acts as a divine share which, when paid, validates the remainder of the mixed wealth, offering a merciful alternative to complex accounting of specific haram portions. The narration underscores the spiritual significance of Khums not merely as a tax, but as a mechanism for spiritual purification and legal clarity in personal finance.
